chapters.title: Jude
body: Jude changes plans mid-letter: he meant to write about "the common salvation" and instead finds himself urging readers to "earnestly contend for the faith," because certain people had "crept in unawares," twisting grace into an excuse for immorality. He reaches back through Israel's history, fallen angels, and Sodom — not for shock value, but because the pattern of ignoring warning signs has already played out before, with real consequences.

Even writing this urgently, Jude doesn't end in alarm — he ends in one of the New Testament's most quoted doxologies: "now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy." Vigilance against real danger and genuine confidence in being kept aren't competing instincts here; Jude holds both in the same short letter, and asks you to as well.
